units.title: Basic Economics Concepts
units.intro: **Scarcity:** wants exceed what resources can make. That forces **choice**. The next-best thing you drop is **opportunity cost**. Economics studies how people, firms and governments choose under scarcity to satisfy material wants as well as they can.

f1.title: On the curve = efficient. Inside = wasted resources. Outside = impossible today. Growth pushes the curve out.

cards.title: 1.0 Introduction to Economics
body: The choices that individuals and societies make in response to scarcity are the subject matter of economics.
Economics is the science of making choices with the objective to meet human wants as much as possible.
Economics is the study of how individuals and societies choose to use their scarce resources in order to satisfy their material wants as much as possible.
Economics is a social science concerned with the efficient use of limited (scarce) resources to achieve maximum satisfaction of human material wants.
Scarcity will always exist and cannot be eliminated in all societies; it is a universal economic problem.

cards.title: Formula
body: Opportunity cost = value of the next-best alternative
Not “everything you could have done” — only the best rejected option.

cards.title: Introduction to Economics
body: **Three questions:** what to produce, how, for whom. **Factors:** land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship. Systems: traditional, command, market, mixed. Most countries are mixed — markets plus a government that taxes, spends and sets rules.

cards.title: 1.1 Production of Goods and Services
body: In order to satisfy human wants, goods and services have to be produced.
Production of goods and services requires efficient use of resources (inputs).
Production is the transformation of inputs into outputs by business firms.
In economics, production involves the processing of raw materials into finished products such as the processing of skin into shoes and other leather products; cotton into textiles or clothes.
Resources used for the production of goods and services have three main characteristics: i.

cards.title: More depth
body: Positive statements = what is (can check). Normative = what ought to be (value). Micro = one market / firm / household. Macro = the whole economy. Specialisation and trade raise output if people do what they are relatively better at — even a low-productivity person can have comparative advantage.

cards.title: 1.2 Business Organizations
body: In their daily life individuals consume various goods and services.
Business organisations sell their goods and services to buyers in the marketplace to earn profits, while buyers purchase them to satisfy their wants.
Business organization refers to any private organization which employs factors of production to produce goods and services for profit.
A business organization may be commercial such as grocery; professional such as providing legal service giving; or an industrial organization such as a shoe making firm.
Sole Proprietorship (sole trader) Sole Proprietorship is the simplest form of business.

cards.title: 1.3 Transportation and Communication
body: In the present world no business can survive without modern communication and transportation systems.

People in the different parts of the world are connected by a network of modern transportation and communication systems, which facilitate the movement of goods and people as well as the transfer of information.
Transportation and communication facilitate trade within a country and among the different countries of the world.
In modem societies, it is very rare to find goods being produced in places where they are wanted or fully consumed.
Often, goods are produced in some places, and they are consumed in other places.

glossary.meaning: Scarcity of resources is the inability of societies to produce enough goods and/or services to satisfy all their material wants and needs.
Economics is the science of making choices with the objective to meet human wants as much as possible.
Production is the transformation of inputs into outputs by business firms.
Human capital is the economic characterization of the education and training of workers.
Labour is the most active factor of production.
Opportunity cost is the amount of goods that must be sacrificed to obtain a unit of another good.
Wealth is the sum of all the assets accumulated over time by a society or a country.
Welfare is the state of well-being of a society.
Microeconomics is a branch of economics that studies the economic behavior of individual decisionmaking units such as consumers and business firms.
Corporation is a egal entity, distinct and separate from the individuals who own it.
Transportation is the safe movement of goods (freight) and people from one place to another.
Water transportation is the safe movement of goods and people through the routes of water bodies such ocean, sea, river, lake or canal.
Air transportation is the safe movement of goods and people from one place to another using air routes.
Communication is the transfer (or exchange) of any kind of information from one person or place to another person or place.
Communication system is a combination of processes and hardware (instruments) used to accomplish the transfer of information (communication).

tips.text: The basic problem of any society is how to use its available resources to meet its wants.
Scarcity of resources is the basic fact of life.
Available resources (factors of production) are scarce in relation to our desires for goods and services.
Resources everywhere are in limited supply (scarce). These questions are answered in different ways under different economic systems.
Economic system refers to the way a society allocates its resources and makes the three economic decisions.
The three economic systems differ in the method of allocating the resources and ownership of the resources.
Production is the process by which factors of production (scarce resources) are changed into goods and services demanded by a society.
The major factors of production are land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.
Land is considered as fixed in quantity.
Society uses resources or factors of production to produce various goods and services to satisfy human wants.
Formula: Opportunity cost = value of the next-best alternative Not “everything you could have done” — only the best rejected option.

units.title: Money and Financial Institutions
units.intro:
Barter needs a double coincidence of wants. Money kills that problem. Functions: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value (and sometimes standard of deferred payment). Good money is durable, portable, divisible, scarce, acceptable.

Banks take deposits, keep a fraction as reserve, lend the rest — that is how credit multiplies (school picture). Central bank (or the state’s bank) issues notes, holds reserves, tries to keep the currency trusted. Other institutions: insurance, microfinance, savings groups — the book’s local list.

cards.title: 2.1 Money
body: During primitive modes of production, each community produces for its own needs.
For example, farmers concentrate on farming, herders concentrate on cattle raising, shoe makers concentrate on making shoes, etc.
Before the introduction of money, there was a system of trading known as barter.
Exchange is the process of obtaining desirable objects by offering something else in return.
The existence of the primitive barter economy shows that exchange was possible without money.

cards.title: MUSE
body: Medium, Unit of account, Store of value, (deferred) Exchange settlement. Inflation steals the store-of-value job — too much money chasing goods.

cards.title: More depth
body: Commodity money (gold, salt, cattle) vs token / fiat (the note is money because the law and trust say so). Cheques and electronic transfers are claims on bank money. Liquidity = how fast an asset becomes spending power without losing value. Cash is most liquid; a building is not.

cards.title: 2.2 Banks and Banking Activities
body: The financial system moves the economy’s scarce resources from savers (people who spend less than they earn) to borrowers (people who spend more than they earn).
Savers save for various reasons—to meet unforeseen emergencies or to live comfortably during retirement age.
Savers supply their money to the financial system and they will get back the principal with interest at a later date.
Borrowers demand money from the financial system and they will be required to pay back the principal and interest at a later date.
The financial system is made up of various financial institutions.

cards.title: Formula
body: Interest = price of borrowed money
Simple I = Prt (Grade 11 maths also). Savers receive interest; borrowers pay it.

cards.title: 2.3 Insurance
body: Individuals face different types of losses or damages for different reasons.
Others will experience destruction of their homes and personal property because of fire, floods, earthquake or other disasters.
Still others will become disabled because of heart disease, cancer, AIDS, or other diseases.
Risk is defined as uncertainty concerning the occurrence of a loss.
For example, the risk of being killed in an accident is present because uncertainty is present.

glossary.meaning: Barter is the exchange of goods for goods without the use of money.
Money is a stock of quantities measured at a particular point in time.
Inflation occurs when there is a general rise in prices without a corresponding increase in productivity.
Deflation is a decline in general price levels, often caused by a reduction in the supply of money or credit.
A central bank is the only authorized bank by law to print money.
Store of value In any society, there is a need to hold wealth in some form or another.
Risk is defined as uncertainty concerning the occurrence of a loss.
Insurance is defined as a form of cooperation through which all those who are open to risks and losses pool their resources and compensate those who suffer a loss.
Therefore, paper money is a legal tender because the law obliges everybody in society to accept it in payment of goods and services as well as in payment of debts.
Exchange is the process of obtaining desirable objects by offering something else in return.
Income is a flow variable measured over a period of time.
Liquidity is the relative ease and speed with which an asset can be converted into cash.
Financial markets are the institutions through which a person who wants to save can directly supply funds to a person who wants to borrow.
Banks are the financial intermediaries with which people are most familiar.
Deposits are the amount of money put in a bank by a customer.
Pooling is the spreading of losses incurred by the few over the entire group, so that in the process, average loss is substituted for actual loss.

tips.text: Before the introduction of money, there was a system of exchange called barter.
Barter is defined as the exchange of goods for goods without the use of money.
The functioning of a barer economy was, however, difficult and inconvenient.

The problems of the barter exchange include the absence of double coincidence of wants, lack of standard measurement during transaction, lack of divisibility, difficulty of storage, etc. These problems made barter a cumbersome and inefficient means of exchange.
The problems encountered and the inefficiency observed in a barter economy led to the invention of money.
Money is defined as anything that is generally accepted in payment for goods and services or in payment of debts.
The introduction of money in an economy solved the problems of barter and facilitated the exchange of goods and services and made efficiency and specialization possible.
Money has four basic functions in an economy: (i) as a medium of exchange, (ii) as a unit of account, (iii) as a store of value, and (iv) as a standard of deferred payments.
Different forms of money have been used in different periods of time in different societies.
Commodity money was the first form to be used to facilitate transaction.
Formula: Interest = price of borrowed money Simple I = Prt (Grade 11 maths also). Savers receive interest; borrowers pay it.

units.title: Bookkeeping for a Service Business
units.intro: A service firm sells time and skill, not a stock of goods (a clinic, a barber, a tutor). Still needs a record of cash, equipment, debts, owner’s stake, income and expenses.

f2.title: Cash received is a debit to Cash (asset up). Service income is a credit (equity up).

lessons.title: Starting an Accounting System for a Business

cards.title: 3.1 Starting an Accounting System for a Business
body: An understanding of the principles of accounting is essential for anyone who is interested in a successful career in business and everyday personal life.
The main purpose of accounting is to provide information concerning the financial affairs of a business.
Accounting is the art of planning how to keep financial records, summarizing, interpreting, and analyzing them to advise what should be done.

Accounting is defined as “the process of identifying, measuring, and communicating economic information to permit informed judgments and decisions by the users of information.” This information is primarily financial-stated in money terms (Nakfa).
Reliable financial information is necessary for sound management decision making.

cards.title: 3.2 Analysis of Business Transactions
body: Dehab established a modern accounting system for her business, Dehab Taxi Services.
The opening entry was journalized in a General Journal and posted to each account in a ledger of Dehab Taxi Services.
The opening balance sheet shows the financial position of the business a at specific date; for example; September 1, current year for Dehab Tax Services.
From time to time the owner of a business wants to know how well his/her business is doing.
An owner wants to know if he/she is making profit or a loss.

lessons.title: Journalizing in General Journal and Posting

cards.title: 3.3 Journalizing in General Journal and Posting
body: Many people write daily events of their life in diaries.
Analysis of business transactions helps in recording entries in a journal.
The historical cost principle specifies that assets acquired by a business entity are to be recorded at the price paid for them.
The price the buyer pays in exchange for an asset is known as the historical cost.
Evidence of the exchange price agreed upon can be found in documents such as purchase invoices, sales invoices, property deeds, transfers of title and other similar documents.

cards.title: Formula
body: Assets = Liabilities + Owner’s equity
Every transaction hits at least two accounts (double entry). Debit left, credit right. DEAD: Debit Expenses, Assets, Drawings. CLIC: Credit Liabilities, Income, Capital.

cards.title: Cash received is a debit to Cash (asset up). Service income is a credit (equity up).
Journalizing in General Journal and Posting
body: Source documents → journal → ledger T-accounts → trial balance (Dr total = Cr total) → simple income statement (income − expenses = profit) → statement of financial position (the accounting equation on a date).

cards.title: Transaction recipe
body: 1 What arrived / left? 2 Which two (or more) accounts? 3 Up or down? 4 DEAD or CLIC? 5 Amounts equal.

cards.title: Worked micro-set
body: Owner starts with 10 000 cash capital. Dr Cash 10 000, Cr Capital 10 000. Pays 2 000 rent. Dr Rent expense 2 000, Cr Cash 2 000. Earns 5 000 cash fees. Dr Cash 5 000, Cr Service income 5 000. Trial: Cash 13 000 Dr; Rent 2 000 Dr; Income 5 000 Cr; Capital 10 000 Cr. Profit = 5 000 − 2 000 = 3 000. Equity ends 13 000. Assets 13 000. Books balance.

lessons.title: Journalizing Transactions in a Cash Journal and Posting

cards.title: 3.4 Journalizing Transactions in a Cash Journal and Posting
body: First, recording all transactions in the General journal would seriously limit the number of transactions that could be processed in a day, simply because only one person at a time could make entries.
Second, transactions recorded in a General journal must be posted individually, resulting in a great deal of posting labour.
A journal that is used to record only one type of transaction is called a special journal.
To facilitate the recording and summarizing process, many businesses, in addition to General journal, use special journals.
The cash journal has a special amount column for each account that is debited or credited frequently.

lessons.title: The Trial Balance and the Work Sheet

cards.title: 3.5 The Trial Balance and the Work Sheet
body: The proof of the equality of the debits and credits in the ledger is called trial balance.
A business analyses its financial condition and prepares financial statements at regular intervals.
The length of time for which an analysis of business operations is made is called a fiscal period (accounting period).
Fiscal periods may consist of a month, a quarter of a year, a half year, or a year.
An accounting period of twelve consecutive months is called a fiscal year.

lessons.title: Financial Statements, Closing the Ledger and Post Closing Trial Balance

cards.title: 3.6 Financial Statements, Closing the Ledger and Post Closing Trial Balance
body: Business entities communicate their financial information to interested users through published financial statements.
Financial statements are designed to provide users with information concerning the profitability and solvency (the capacity to pay debts of business entities).
When the total income exceeds the total expense the difference is called net income (profit).
When the total expenses exceed the total income, the difference is called net loss (loss).
Revenue is the amount charged for goods or services rendered.

glossary.meaning: Accounting is the art of planning how to keep financial records, summarizing, interpreting, and analyzing them to advise what should be done.
The balance sheet accounts are called permanent, capital or real accounts.
Bookkeeping is the art of recording financial activities.
Each record in a journal is called an entry.
A business transaction is an exchange of property or service.
Note that in a general journal, the left hand amount column is the debit and the right amount column is the credit.
The left hand side of an account is called debit side.
Posting is the transfer of amounts from journals to the ledger.

Article 80 (1): The capital is the original value of the elements put at the disposal of the undertaking by the owner by way of contributions in cash or in kind.
Debit side account is called the …………… G.
To credit an account means to enter an amount on the right, or credit, side.
Post Reference is a column reserved for writing the account number to which the data on the journal is transferred.
Cash is the first account to be opened in the ledger of the Dehab Taxi Service business.
Revenue and expense accounts are called temporary accounts or nominal accounts.
Depreciation is the process of allocating the cost of an asset to expense over its useful service years in a rational and systematic manner.
Revenue is the amount charged for goods or services rendered.

tips.text: From time to time, the owner of a business wants to know how well his/her business is doing.
An owner wants to know if he/she is profiting or losing money.
In order to determine whether a business operation has resulted in net profit or net loss, every business transaction is recorded in a journal.

Prior to journalizing, business transactions are analysed using a financial transaction work sheet to determine the transactions effect on the accounting equation and facilitate recording journal entries.

In this sub-unit, we illustrated the analysis of business transactions such as: additional investment of capital by the owner of the business; purchase of an asset for cash; purchase of an asset on account; part payment of a liability; sale of an asset for cash; income transactions and expense transactions.
In the following sub-unit, we will record the business transactions in a General Journal.
Businesses use specialized journals to record frequent business transactions such as cash receipt and cash payments.
A special journal in which only cash transactions (cash receipts and cash payments) are recorded is called a cash journal.
The use of a cash journal in service business helps to save space and time in recording and posting entries. Moreover, it helps in proving the cash on hand.
In addition to the cash journal businesses use a general journal to record transactions that do not affect cash (for example, the purchase of an asset when agreeing to pay in the future).
